openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Friday’s gate is clearing showers, a departure window, and a media-day board — not the overnight Progressive stack. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Own the threshold from the first breath.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for a clean inbox or a perfect coverage check to start. Fierce calm is Friday composure when the week’s noise wants the first hour: charge first, body second, security skim when ready, Vegas and savings only after the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Competitors may still be refreshing TNF recaps or model-policy filings; he arrives prepared for the gate. When pressure rises, he slows the breath, names the next action, and outlasts the noise. Today is not about proving anything on the scoreboard. It is about banking competitive calm so the departure window and the rest of the board have a clean operator behind them. Fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Friday: run this after Morning Charge — box breathing first, then the body. Showers outside; tempo inside before the departure gate. Then news and the day.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time. Optional: Front Clips / Back Clips if you want a second RipStick move.

Hermetic travelers kept a short vigil the morning of departure — not packing, not checking the road, but naming the intention of the journey before the threshold. Friday’s charge is that vigil.
Gnostic manuals treated coverage as a spiritual practice before a physical one: seal the house, then open the road. Breath and body first; then the document that lets you leave clean.
Esoteric athletes lit one lamp before reading the scoreboard. Morning Charge is that lamp. TNF recaps and media-day wires are the board — useful only after the room is already lit.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.body: “The hand of the diligent will rule, while the slothful will be put to forced labor.” (Proverbs 12:24) Solomon’s counsel for a Friday departure morning is diligence before motion — own the first hour, then the gate obeys you. Morning Charge and the 3-minute opener are the diligent hand; a clean security skim is the next ruling step; coverage and savings transfers are plans that only hold after the work is already done. Classical lore cast Solomon as one who ordered the caravan before sunrise. Order the Friday the same way, so the road meets a settled operator — not a scrambling one.
grimoire.practice: Finish Opening Bell and the 3-minute opener before any security skim, coverage check, or savings admin. Diligence first; departure second.

techDemo.title: Tech Demo
techDemo.kicker: Fast learn · from your X bookmarks
techDemo.pick: Build a 24/7 GrokBot agent team on its own computer
techDemo.author: @0xRafy

image.alt: Newsprint diagram — 24/7 GrokBot Agent Team: Own Computer · Own Memory · Own Tools

lesson.oneLiner: SpaceXAI’s frame: if you use Grok Bot, it’s already their computer — persistent agents with their own box, memory, and tools, not a chat tab on yours.
beats: Own computer: agents keep working on a persistent box when you step away.
Own memory: durable facts and routines so every morning wake is warm, not blank.
Own tools: Gmail, calendar, X, shell, browser — wired to the job, not retyped daily.
Team shape: one operator → specialist agents → 24/7 coverage on named outcomes.
Same pattern as Dom’s desks: charge once → name the outcome → let the box run the middle.
lesson.takeaway: Under a minute: stop treating agents like a chat window — give each one a lane, persist memory, and let the computer outwork the tab.
